cues.en: I'm Bruce Bugbee. I'm a professor of crop physiology at Utah State University,
cues.zh: 我是 Bruce Bugbee，犹他州立大学作物生理学教授，

cues.en: and this is a seminar about calculating potential yield of any agricultural commodity.
cues.zh: 这场讲座讲的是如何计算任何农产品的潜在产量。

cues.en: It was first developed for fields like this and for outdoor agriculture.
cues.zh: 它最初是为像这样的田地、为户外农业开发的。

cues.en: But over the years, we have modified this model, which is a series of calculations, to get potential yield in indoor agriculture.
cues.zh: 但多年来，我们修改了这个模型——它是一系列计算——用来得出室内农业的潜在产量。

cues.en: And as we get better and better with indoor agriculture, it becomes increasingly important to understand what the potential is.
cues.zh: 而随着我们在室内农业上越来越成熟，理解其潜力就变得越来越重要。

cues.en: In this talk, in the next 20-25 minutes, I'm going to just derive the potential yield from what we call first principles.
cues.zh: 在这场演讲中，接下来20到25分钟里，我将从我们所说的第一性原理出发，推导潜在产量。

cues.en: But first I want to acknowledge the funding agencies for this, and NASA is a key funding agency.
cues.zh: 但首先，我要感谢为本研究提供资助的机构，NASA是其中的关键资助机构。

cues.en: They’ve funded the research in my lab for over 30 years, and we've been deeply indebted to NASA for allowing us to keep refining these models.
cues.zh: 他们资助我实验室的研究已超过30年，我们深深感激NASA让我们能够不断改进这些模型。

cues.en: Recently, we also got funded by the USDA.
cues.zh: 最近，我们也获得了USDA的资助。

cues.en: And this is a project, much more applied project, to look at the use of supplemental lighting in controlled environments.
cues.zh: 这是一个项目，更偏应用，研究在受控环境中使用补光。

cues.en: This project is called the LAMP project: “Lighting Approaches to Maximize Profits.”
cues.zh: 这个项目叫 LAMP 项目，即“Lighting Approaches to Maximize Profits”（最大化利润的照明方法）。

cues.en: So this is a very basic research project. This is a very applied research project.
cues.zh: 所以这是一个非常基础的研究项目。这是一个非常偏应用的研究项目。

cues.en: And back-and-forth, we zero in on the reality of what we can get for food production in controlled environments.
cues.zh: 通过反复来回，我们聚焦于在受控环境中进行食品生产时实际能做到什么。

cues.en: So let's now show you the units of this calculation.
cues.zh: 那么现在让我们展示一下这个计算的单位。

cues.en: One gram per mole of photons.
cues.zh: 每摩尔光子一克。

cues.en: This is an output from the system. One gram of dry biomass, or one gram of yield, per mole of photosynthetic photons.
cues.zh: 这是系统的产出。每摩尔光合光子对应一克干生物量，也就是一克产量。

cues.en: So it's output divided by input, which is the efficiency of the system.
cues.zh: 所以就是产出除以投入，也就是系统的效率。

cues.en: Now just quickly I can show you how we derive this--and let's make sure we're on black.
cues.zh: 现在快速演示一下我们是怎么推导出它的——先确认现在是黑底。

cues.en: One gram, let's put it right over here.
cues.zh: 一克，就放在这里。

cues.en: A gram per meter² of ground area per day, divided by a mole of photons per meter² of ground area per day.
cues.zh: 每平方米地面面积每天一克，除以每平方米地面面积每天一摩尔光子。

cues.en: And you can see, the meter², the days cancel out, and we get grams per mole.
cues.zh: 可以看到，平方米和天相互抵消，得到克每摩尔。

cues.en: This mole per meter² right here is called the daily light integral.
cues.zh: 这里的每平方米摩尔数称为每日光积分。

cues.en: DLI. It's a common measurement, moles per meter squared per day.
cues.zh: DLI。它是一种常见度量，单位是摩尔每平方米每天。

cues.en: This is just biomass. This is tricky calculating the exact area because we get guard row effects.
cues.zh: 这只是生物量。精确计算面积很棘手，因为会遇到保护行效应。

cues.en: But these are the input parameters to this. Now, where do these come from and how can we calculate yield?
cues.zh: 但这些是它的输入参数。那么，这些从哪来，我们又该如何计算产量？

cues.en: I want to start by examining what to any plant biologist is the most important equation in the world.
cues.zh: 我想先来看看，对任何植物生物学家来说，世界上最重要的方程是什么。

cues.en: Now, when I show this to physicist colleagues, they're pretty sure the most important equation in the world is E = mc².
cues.zh: 现在，我把这个拿给物理学家同事看时，他们很确定世界上最重要的方程是 E = mc²。

cues.en: What do you think this is? The most important equation in the world, particularly to any life scientist? Here it is.
cues.zh: 你们觉得这是什么？世界上最重要的方程，尤其对任何生命科学家来说？就是这个。

cues.en: Equations are inputs, and they go to outputs.
cues.zh: 方程是输入，然后变成输出。

cues.en: Now this is in every single high school biology textbook. It's in every textbook in college.
cues.zh: 这在每一本高中生物课本里都有，在大学教材里也都有。

cues.en: We have 20 courses on college campuses that emphasize this equation. Of course it helps to know what this is.
cues.zh: 我们在大学校园里开设了20门课程，都在强调这个方程式。当然，知道这是什么会有帮助。

cues.en: That is carbohydrate, CH₂O.
cues.zh: 那就是碳水化合物，CH₂O。

cues.en: And this equation, by now you've figured it out, this is photosynthesis.
cues.zh: 而这个方程式，你们现在应该已经看出来了，就是光合作用。

cues.en: So now we look at this.
cues.zh: 那现在我们来看这个。

cues.en: This takes a low--let's get a different color here--this takes a low-energy gas, CO₂. We use it to put out fires. And water.
cues.zh: 这个反应吸收一种低能——我换个颜色——吸收一种低能气体，CO₂。我们用它来灭火。还有水。

cues.en: Two really simple molecules. Very low energy. And it makes a high-energy solid food and, well, O₂ is rocket fuel.
cues.zh: 两个非常简单的分子。能量很低。它生成一种高能量的固体食物，而且，O₂可是火箭燃料。

cues.en: So we get two very high energy outputs from two very low energy inputs. We often we don't think about that a lot.
cues.zh: 所以我们从两个能量很低的输入，得到了两个能量很高的输出。我们常常不太会去想这一点。

cues.en: We make students memorize the stoichiometry, but the energetics of this is what's really important.
cues.zh: 我们让学生去背化学计量关系，但真正重要的是这里的能量变化。

cues.en: Now, remember the first law of thermodynamics says "energy in equals energy out".
cues.zh: 记住，热力学第一定律说的是"能量输入等于能量输出"。

cues.en: Everything has to follow the first law. How do we get two really low input molecules to go to two high input molecules?
cues.zh: 一切都必须遵守第一定律。那我们怎么让两个能量很低的输入分子，变成两个能量很高的分子呢？

cues.en: The answer is, in more advanced books, light. And particularly photons. And particularly 10 photons.
cues.zh: 答案是，在更高级的教材里，是光。尤其是光子。尤其是 10 个光子。

cues.en: This is close to the theoretical minimum number of photons to push this equation across.
cues.zh: 这已经接近让这个方程成立所需的理论最少光子数。

cues.en: So, how are we going to derive grams per mole of photons from this 10 photons?
cues.zh: 那么，我们如何从这 10 个光子推导出每摩尔光子的克数？

cues.en: Every book has this in it. The advanced books have the photons.
cues.zh: 每本书里都有这个；高级教材里才有光子。

cues.en: This has always disturbed me that it's written like this because it doesn't capture, for our students, the magnificence of this equation and how you get these high energy outputs.
cues.zh: 它这样写一直让我不安，因为对学生来说，它没有展现出这个方程的壮丽，以及这些高能输出是怎么来的。

cues.en: So, I would like to propose that we revise the way we write this equation.
cues.zh: 所以，我想提议我们改一下这个方程式的写法。

cues.en: Here's the earth… BOOM!
cues.zh: 这是地球……砰！

cues.en: Here is our low energy inputs, and here is our high energy outputs. And it's many steps to get up there.
cues.zh: 这里是我们的低能量输入，这里是我们的高能量输出。要爬上去得经过很多步。

cues.en: And now, how do you get uphill from low energy to high? We bring in those 10 photons… KABOOM!
cues.zh: 那么，怎么从低能量爬升到高能量呢？我们引入那 10 个光子……轰！

cues.en: There’s a lot of energy in those photons. Now the energy balances because the 10 photons drive it uphill.
cues.zh: 那些光子里蕴含着大量能量。现在能量平衡了，因为这 10 个光子把它推了上去。

cues.en: When we calculate the efficiency of this, and efficiency is--I'm going to abbreviate it--I'll write it out.
cues.zh: 当我们计算它的效率时，效率是——我把它缩写一下——我写出来。

cues.en: Efficiency of any system is just the output over the input.
cues.zh: 任何系统的效率，就是输出除以输入。

cues.en: So the output is carbohydrate, and the input is 10 photons.
cues.zh: 所以输出是碳水化合物，输入是 10 个光子。

cues.en: When we do this ratio, we get 30% efficient, in theory. Here it is. Theoretical maximum 30%.
cues.zh: 算这个比值，理论上效率是 30%。看，理论最大值就是 30%。

cues.en: That doesn't sound very good for a theoretical maximum.
cues.zh: 作为理论最大值，这听起来可不太好。

cues.en: And engineers look at this and say, “Oh my goodness! 30%? That's all your important equation can do?”
cues.zh: 工程师们一看就说：“天哪！30%？你那个重要公式就只能算出这个？”

cues.en: And it's bothered me for a while.
cues.zh: 这事困扰了我一阵子。

cues.en: So then I thought, wait a minute! I look at the biochemistry, and this is not one big step.
cues.zh: 于是我想，等一下！我看看生物化学过程，这可不是一步完成的。

cues.en: This is many, many little steps. This goes to this, and then this goes to this.
cues.zh: 这是很多很多的小步骤。这个变成这个，然后这个变成这个。

cues.en: When we start to add up all those steps,
cues.zh: 当我们把所有那些步骤累加起来，

cues.en: if you assume there's 23 steps, and that's about right, and each step is 95% efficient, now look at the math in this.
cues.zh: 假设有 23 步——这个数字差不多是对的——而每一步的效率是 95%，现在来看看这里面的数学。

cues.en: If we take point .95 to the 23rd power, that's 30% efficient.
cues.zh: 0.95 的 23 次方，效率就只有 30%。

cues.en: So we should start thinking about photosynthesis as 23-automated steps, each one's 95% efficient,
cues.zh: 所以我们应该把光合作用看成 23 个自动化步骤，每一步的效率是 95%，

cues.en: and out the end we get carbohydrates and food energy.
cues.zh: 最终我们得到碳水化合物和食物能量。

cues.en: This is where this whole analysis comes from is this equation balancing. Now, let's look at these 10 photons.
cues.zh: 整个分析就是从这种方程式配平来的。现在，我们来看这 10 个光子。

cues.en: That's the theoretical minimum. How close can we get to that when we measure this in a plant?
cues.zh: 那是理论最小值。我们在植物中测量时，能接近它到什么程度？

cues.en: Here's a graph of photosynthetic photon flux density down here. Increasing light, zero is dark, go all the way up to 1,000.
cues.zh: 下面这张图是光合光子通量密度。光照逐渐增强，0 是黑暗，一直到 1,000。

cues.en: And this is the quantum yield. So this ratio, moles of carbon fixed per mole of photons absorbed, is called quantum yield.
cues.zh: 这就是量子产率。这个比值，即每吸收一摩尔光子所固定的碳的摩尔数，称为量子产率。

cues.en: Remember I said 10? 10 is called the quantum requirement to this. So one over 10 is 0.10.
cues.zh: 还记得我说过的 10 吗？10 被称为它的量子需要量。所以 1 除以 10 就是 0.10。

cues.en: So same thing just different units. Now look at this. We can't quite get to 10, but we get close up here.
cues.zh: 所以是一回事，只是单位不同。现在看这个。我们没法完全达到 10，但在这里已经很接近了。

cues.en: The type of plant really doesn't matter as long as it's a nice green leaf. Tomato. Spinach.
cues.zh: 植物是什么类型其实不重要，只要是健康的绿叶就行。番茄。菠菜。

cues.en: Different kind of tomato. In this case, Grand Rapids leaf is quite a light yellow leaf, and it had a little bit lower quantum yield.
cues.zh: 另一种番茄。这里，Grand Rapids 的叶片相当浅黄，量子产率也略低一些。

cues.en: Now when I say the leaf doesn't matter, purple.
cues.zh: 现在我说叶子不重要时，指的是紫色。

cues.en: Purple leaf lettuce, that is full of anthocyanins, and anthocyanins are a protective pigment in leaves.
cues.zh: 紫叶生菜富含花青素，而花青素是叶片中的保护性色素。

cues.en: They absorb solar energy, and they don't fix carbon in photosynthesis.
cues.zh: 它们吸收太阳能，但在光合作用中不固定碳。

cues.en: So when we have purple leaf cultivars, their quantum yield is fundamentally less than nice green leaf cultivars.
cues.zh: 所以对于紫叶品种，其量子产率本质上低于优质绿叶品种。

cues.en: We only get to these very low, very high quantum yields and very low light.
cues.zh: 只有在光照极低时，我们才会得到这些极低、极高的量子产率。

cues.en: So if we're gonna be more real about this, let's assume that we're growing the plants at 400 micromoles. It’s more typical.
cues.zh: 那如果我们更贴近实际一点，就假设植物在 400 微摩尔下生长。这更典型。

cues.en: And we go up here. And we go across here. And we're at a quantum yield of 0.08 and quantum requirement of 12.
cues.zh: 然后往上到这里，再横向到这里。我们得到量子产率 0.08、量子需要量 12。

cues.en: So let's take this now and refine our model of grams per mole of photons.
cues.zh: 那现在拿这个来细化我们“每摩尔光子对应多少克”的模型。

cues.en: There's 400 µmols.
cues.zh: 这里有 400 微摩尔。

cues.en: We know that carbohydrate is 30 grams per mole. This is pretty simple.
cues.zh: 我们知道碳水化合物是每摩尔 30 克。这很简单。

cues.en: Carbohydrate is 12. Hydrogen adds two. Oxygen adds 16. That's 30 grams per mole.
cues.zh: 碳是 12。氢加 2。氧加 16。这样就是每摩尔 30 克。

cues.en: 12 moles of photons gives us 30 grams of biomass, and the efficiency of this system then, output over input, is 30 grams per 12 moles = 2.5 grams.
cues.zh: 12 摩尔光子能产生 30 克生物量，那么这个系统的效率，也就是输出除以输入，就是 30 克除以 12 摩尔 = 2.5 克。

cues.en: This is significantly higher than what we talked about a minute ago is one gram per mole of photons.
cues.zh: 这比我们一分钟前说的每摩尔光子一克要高得多。

cues.en: What's the difference in this? The key here is that this is one way.
cues.zh: 差别在哪？关键在于这是单向的。

cues.en: When we run this in the light, the first stable product out of photosynthesis is not just carbohydrate, it’s sucrose.
cues.zh: 当我们在光照下运行这个过程时，光合作用产生的第一个稳定产物不只是碳水化合物，而是蔗糖。

cues.en: If we're only running at one direction, we get sucrose, and even sugarcane is not pure sucrose.
cues.zh: 如果我们只朝一个方向运行，得到的是蔗糖，而即便是甘蔗也不是纯蔗糖。

cues.en: We have proteins in plants, lipids, lignin, cellulose, all kinds of things. How do those things get made, if we're running this only to get sucrose?
cues.zh: 植物里有蛋白质、脂质、木质素、纤维素等各种物质。如果只为了得到蔗糖而运行这个过程，那这些东西是怎么生成的？

cues.en: They get made at night, and they get made continuously by running this equation backwards.
cues.zh: 它们在夜间生成，并且通过反向运行这个方程持续生成。

cues.en: This direction, and then we get ATP energy.
cues.zh: 朝这个方向运行，然后我们就得到 ATP 能量。

cues.en: And that ATP is used to synthesize all the other things in plants.
cues.zh: 这些 ATP 用来合成植物中所有其他物质。

cues.en: When we run it backwards, we call it respiration.
cues.zh: 当它反向运行时，我们称之为呼吸作用。

cues.en: So respiration takes about 40% of this. After we get here, about 40% is run backwards to make everything else in plants.
cues.zh: 所以呼吸作用大约占其中的40%。到达这一步后，大约40%会反向运行，用来生成植物中的其他所有成分。

cues.en: We can measure this rigorously by canopy gas exchange. This is a picture of some of our chambers.
cues.zh: 我们可以通过冠层气体交换来严格测量这一点。这是我们部分气室的照片。

cues.en: They're little transparent chambers. We measure the gases coming in and out. We keep track of all the CO₂ in this system.
cues.zh: 它们是小型的透明气室。我们测量进出气室的气体。我们追踪这个系统中所有的 CO₂。

cues.en: And we can keep track of the exact number of photons from minute-to-minute.
cues.zh: 而且我们能逐分钟追踪光子的精确数量。

cues.en: The exact rate of sucrose production, and then respiration. Now respiration runs in the light and the dark all the time.
cues.zh: 蔗糖的精确生成速率，然后是呼吸作用。呼吸作用在光照和黑暗中一直都在进行。

cues.en: So it's running back and forth. So we never get 2.5 grams of biomass. That would only be sucrose.
cues.zh: 所以它来回运转。所以我们永远得不到2.5克生物量。那只会是蔗糖。

cues.en: How efficient is respiration? 60%.
cues.zh: 呼吸作用的效率有多高？60%。

cues.en: I'm off the edge of the screen, I need to go back--60%.
cues.zh: 我跑到屏幕边缘外了，我得回去——60%。

cues.en: Respiration is net photosynthesis divided by gross photosynthesis.
cues.zh: 呼吸作用等于净光合作用除以总光合作用。

cues.en: We also call that daily carbon gain divided by gross photosynthesis. That ratio’s about 60.
cues.zh: 我们也把它叫作每日碳增益除以总光合作用。这个比例大约是60。

cues.en: 60, how do we get up to that number?
cues.zh: 60，我们怎么才能达到这个数字？

cues.en: Jonathan France was a PhD student with me many years ago, and he spent his whole time studying this.
cues.zh: Jonathan France 很多年前跟我读博士，他把全部时间都花在研究这个上。

cues.en: Couldn't we make respiration more efficient? Couldn't we get this higher than 60%?
cues.zh: 我们能不能让呼吸作用更高效？能不能把它提高到 60% 以上？

cues.en: And we eventually did. We got it to like 65%. We couldn't improve it much. Cold nights. Long days. Continuous light.
cues.zh: 最终我们做到了，大概到了 65%。但也没能再提高多少。冷夜、长日、连续光照。

cues.en: We were close to fixed at 60%.
cues.zh: 我们基本就卡在 60% 附近了。

cues.en: So now we take 2.5 grams, going this way, times 60% equals, now we're down to 1.5 grams per mole.
cues.zh: 所以现在我们取 2.5 克，按这个方向算，乘以 60%，等于——现在降到每摩尔 1.5 克。

cues.en: And we call this number Photon Conversion Efficacy or PCE.
cues.zh: 我们把这个数值称为光子转换效率，简称 PCE。

cues.en: So, in the first slide I said we can get one gram per mole of photons. This is 1.5 grams.
cues.zh: 在第一张幻灯片里我说过，每摩尔光子可以产出 1 克。而这里是 1.5 克。

cues.en: But this number assumes every photon gets absorbed by the plants. None of them bounce off. None of them hit the ground.
cues.zh: 但这个数字假设每个光子都被植物吸收了。没有光子被反射，也没有光子落到地面。

cues.en: 100% of the photons get absorbed. And that never happens.
cues.zh: 100% 的光子都被吸收。而这种情况永远不会发生。

cues.en: Even in a perfect canopy, a few percent bounce off and go back up to the ceiling.
cues.zh: 即使是在完美的冠层中，也有几个百分点的光子被反射，回到顶部。

cues.en: Some hit the walls, and even worse, some hit the ground without hitting a leaf and those are completely gone.
cues.zh: 有些撞到了墙上，更糟的是，有些没碰到叶子就落到地面，然后就彻底消失了。

cues.en: To go from this perfect system where we just have photosynthesis and respiration to a real system, we need a little more sophisticated model.
cues.zh: 要从这个只有光合作用和呼吸作用的完美系统，过渡到真实系统，我们需要一个更精细一点的模型。

cues.en: And that sophisticated model is called the Energy Cascade model that I've worked on with other people for many years, and we have several papers about it.
cues.zh: 这个更精细的模型叫 Energy Cascade 模型，我多年来一直和其他人合作研究它，也发表了好几篇相关论文。

cues.en: Here's the model. Here's our two parameters right here that we're talking about.
cues.zh: 这是模型。这里是我们讨论的两个参数。

cues.en: And in this typical case right here, I'm using 0.06 because if it's higher light levels, we get a little lower quantum yield.
cues.zh: 在这个典型情况下，我用 0.06，因为光照水平更高时，量子产率会略低。

cues.en: But the very first step in this model is fraction of absorbed photons.
cues.zh: 但这个模型的第一步是吸收光子的比例。

cues.en: And we're assuming 80%. This number is more like 50% in typical field production,
cues.zh: 我们假设是 80%。在典型田间生产中，这个数字更接近 50%，

cues.en: but with high planting density and maybe systems to move the plants apart, we capture more photons.
cues.zh: 但通过高种植密度，或许还有把植株分开的系统，我们能捕获更多光子。

cues.en: 80% times quantum yield times carbon use efficiency gives us biomass per mole of incident photons.
cues.zh: 80% 乘以量子产率，再乘以碳利用效率，就得到每摩尔入射光子对应的生物量。

cues.en: And finally the fourth one is called harvest index.
cues.zh: 最后，第四个叫收获指数。

cues.en: That's the ratio of usable or edible product to total plant biomass.
cues.zh: 即可用或可食用部分占植物总生物量的比例。

cues.en: In the case of lettuce, this number is 80-85%. We don't eat the roots. We don't eat the stem base. Lettuce is almost completely edible.
cues.zh: 以生菜为例，这个数字是 80–85%。我们不吃根，也不吃茎基部。生菜几乎整株都能吃。

cues.en: But in typical crop plants, we're at 50%. Wheat and rice. That’d be tremendous if we could get those to 50%.
cues.zh: 但在典型作物中，这个比例是 50%。小麦和水稻。如果能让它们达到 50%，那将非常了不起。

cues.en: They're more like 40% typically.
cues.zh: 它们通常在 40% 左右。

cues.en: So we take this. We get moles of carbon fixed per mole of photons,
cues.zh: 我们拿这个来算：每摩尔光子能固定多少摩尔碳，

cues.en: and now we multiply by 30 grams per mole, and we're down to 0.4 grams per mole,
cues.zh: 现在再乘以每摩尔 30 克，就降到每摩尔 0.4 克，

cues.en: well below our one gram per mole that I advertised on that first slide.
cues.zh: 远低于我在第一张幻灯片上说的每摩尔 1 克。

cues.en: So now let's look at potential. What do we have to do to get this up to one?
cues.zh: 现在我们看看潜力。要把它提高到 1，需要做什么？

cues.en: Here's a set of numbers. If we improve each one of these just slightly. We get that 80% absorbed to 90%, slight improvement.
cues.zh: 这里有一组数字。只要把每一项都稍微改进一点，就能把吸收率从 80% 提高到 90%，这是小幅提升。

cues.en: Quantum yield, we get it from 0.06 to 0.08. Low light and--it's one thing to get 0.08, but keep it there over the whole lifecycle.
cues.zh: 量子产率，我们从 0.06 提高到 0.08。弱光下——达到 0.08 是一回事，但要在整个生命周期里保持住是另一回事。

cues.en: When the plants are old, try to still have this high quantum yield.
cues.zh: 当植株衰老时，也要尽量保持这么高的量子产率。

cues.en: Improve carbon use efficiency to 0.65. Go to a very high harvest index crop. Multiply these together.
cues.zh: 把碳利用效率提高到 0.65。采用收获指数很高的作物。把这些乘在一起。

cues.en: Now we're at one gram per mole. There's the magic one gram per mole.
cues.zh: 现在我们达到了每摩尔一克。这就是那个神奇的每摩尔一克。

cues.en: This is the potential yield. And in some systems where we very carefully measure this, we can get one gram per mole.
cues.zh: 这就是潜在产量。在一些我们非常仔细测量这一指标的系统中，我们可以做到每摩尔一克。

cues.en: It is not an average, it's a potential. And you've got to hit it every single day of the lifecycle.
cues.zh: 这不是平均值，而是潜力值。而在整个生命周期里，你每天都得达到它。

cues.en: Very hard to do, but it's still a potential yield.
cues.zh: 这很难做到，但它仍是潜在的产量。

cues.en: Most indoor farms that we have analyzed are down around 0.4 grams per mole now.
cues.zh: 我们分析过的大多数室内农场，目前只有每摩尔0.4克左右。

cues.en: Mostly because they're not absorbing all the light up here. Many of the photons don't fall on leaves.
cues.zh: 主要是因为它们没有吸收上方所有的光。很多光子根本没落在叶片上。

cues.en: By the way, this quantum yield only is achievable with very elevated CO₂. Like 1,200 parts per million. It's 400 outside.
cues.zh: 顺便说一句，这种量子产率只有在二氧化碳浓度很高时才做得到。比如1200ppm。室外只有400。

cues.en: That causes photorespiration. We can't have that. To get to this number you have to have high CO₂.
cues.zh: 那会导致光呼吸。我们不能让这种情况发生。要达到这个数字，必须有高浓度CO₂。

cues.en: It’d be much less than this without high CO₂. But we can enriched with CO₂ in indoor agriculture.
cues.zh: 如果没有高浓度CO₂，这个数字会低得多。但在室内农业中，我们可以通过CO₂来富集。

cues.en: This approach came from this article right here, “Exploring the Limits of Crop productivity,”
cues.zh: 这种方法来自这里的这篇文章——《探索作物生产力的极限》，

cues.en: that I wrote with my colleague Frank Salisbury about, well 1988, that's over 30 years ago.
cues.zh: 那是我和同事 Frank Salisbury 在大约——嗯，1988年写的，已经是30多年前了。

cues.en: This particular article helped launch my career as a young scientist.
cues.zh: 正是这篇文章，帮助我开启了作为年轻科学家的职业生涯。

cues.en: Showing the math, and then showing what we could get to in potential yield.
cues.zh: 展示计算过程，然后看潜在产量能达到什么水平。

cues.en: And of course we did this with wheat and kept track of all those parameters, and that was the basis of the paper.
cues.zh: 当然，我们用小麦做了这个，并跟踪了所有这些参数，这就是那篇论文的基础。

cues.en: So now let's look, after we calculate potential yield, let's do an economic analysis of indoor ag.
cues.zh: 现在看看，算完潜在产量后，我们来做室内农业的经济分析。

cues.en: We know the cost of electricity. If we know we could get one gram per mole, what's the economics of this?
cues.zh: 我们知道电费。如果知道每摩尔能产出1克，这经济性如何？

cues.en: This is, what I'm going to show you on this slide now is the basis from this paper.
cues.zh: 我现在这张幻灯片要展示的，就是这篇论文的基础。

cues.en: It was an article we published in “Nature.” “LEDs for photons, physiology, and food.”
cues.zh: 这是我们发表在《Nature》上的一篇文章：“LEDs for photons, physiology, and food.”

cues.en: This is just last year, 2018.
cues.zh: 就是去年，2018年。

cues.en: Assuming 10 cents a kilowatt-hour, which is a sort of a national average, cost of photons as a percent of the market price.
cues.zh: 假设每千瓦时10美分，这大致是全国平均水平，算一下光子成本占市场价格的百分比。

cues.en: So we took the market price as high as we could get. Gourmet, premium quality lettuce. And look at this, 1% and 5%.
cues.zh: 我们把市场价格尽量往高了取，用高档优质生菜。看这里，1%和5%。

cues.en: No wonder people are rushing to do indoor agriculture for leafy microgreens and for lettuce.
cues.zh: 难怪大家都蜂拥去做室内农业，种叶类微型菜和生菜。

cues.en: But, most of the facilities now where we have 5%, they're at more like 30% of the cost of photons as a percent of market price.
cues.zh: 但现在大多数设施，我们能做到 5% 的，光子成本占市场售价的比例更接近 30%。

cues.en: And that's because the systems are not yet optimized. They can run with 30% energy, but they could get down to 5%.
cues.zh: 这是因为系统还没优化。它们能以 30% 的能耗运行，但能耗可以降到 5%。

cues.en: Now, let's look at tomatoes in this system.
cues.zh: 现在，我们看看这个系统里的番茄。

cues.en: Tomatoes have a much lower harvest index. You throw away the leaves and stems and roots. You only eat the tomatoes.
cues.zh: 番茄的收获指数低得多。叶子、茎和根都要扔掉，只吃番茄。

cues.en: The tomatoes don't have as much water as lettuce. Lettuce is 95% water,
cues.zh: 番茄的水分没有生菜那么多。生菜 95% 是水，

cues.en: and we only need photosynthesis to grow the 5% that's dry weight. But tomatoes are much harder.
cues.zh: 我们只需要光合作用来长那 5% 的干重。但番茄要难得多。

cues.en: When we go to tomatoes we get 18%. It's harder to grow tomatoes than these.
cues.zh: 说到番茄，我们只能得到18%。番茄比这些更难种。

cues.en: Still possible, but boy, we're going to have to have optimal conditions to ever think about growing tomatoes.
cues.zh: 仍然有可能，但天哪，我们得具备最佳条件，才能谈得上种番茄。

cues.en: Now let's look at other vegetables. Let's take broccoli.
cues.zh: 现在看看其他蔬菜。拿西兰花来说。

cues.en: Lots of broccoli we can't sell: stems, leaves, roots, and broccoli is more dry weight and less water.
cues.zh: 很多西兰花我们卖不掉：茎、叶、根，而且西兰花干重更高、水分更少。

cues.en: And it doesn't command the premium price that lettuce and tomatoes do.
cues.zh: 而且它卖不出生菜和番茄那样的高价。

cues.en: General vegetables, the cost of the photons is equal to the market value of the product.
cues.zh: 普通蔬菜，光子成本就等于产品的市场价值。

cues.en: So unless we can find a way to get consumers to pay a lot more for general vegetables,
cues.zh: 所以，除非我们能想办法让消费者为普通蔬菜多付很多钱，

cues.en: including things like strawberries, it's going to be very, very difficult.
cues.zh: 包括草莓这类东西，否则会非常非常困难。

cues.en: And by this analysis, at 10 cents a kilowatt hour, it's not going to be cost-effective.
cues.zh: 而按这个分析，每千瓦时10美分时，它不会划算。

cues.en: The electric cost is going to be equal to the market value, and you still have labor. You have depreciation.
cues.zh: 电费会等于市场价值，而且你还有人工成本，还有折旧。

cues.en: You have lots of other costs besides the photon costs.
cues.zh: 除了光子成本，你还有很多其他成本。

cues.en: Even worse--rice or wheat.
cues.zh: 更糟的是——水稻或小麦。

cues.en: The value of the photons is a hundred times greater than the value of the rice and wheat.
cues.zh: 光子的价值是水稻和小麦价值的一百倍。

cues.en: We are never going to grow our staple crops without sunlight. We need free sunlight to grow these staple crops.
cues.zh: 没有阳光，我们永远种不出主粮作物。我们需要免费的阳光来种这些主粮作物。

cues.en: One way to look at this—the rapidly increasing cost of photons—is the market price.
cues.zh: 看待这件事——光子成本快速上涨——的一个角度是市场价格。

cues.en: These are high market price. These are low market price. That's what drives this cost of photons up.
cues.zh: 这些市场价格高。这些市场价格低。正是这推高了光子成本。

cues.en: And then secondly, the harvest index.
cues.zh: 然后是第二点，收获指数。

cues.en: These have a high harvest index and it decreases down to 50%. There are tomato lines that are 70%.
cues.zh: 这些的收获指数很高，最低会降到50%。有些番茄品系能达到70%。

cues.en: So we could potentially do a little bit better with tomatoes.
cues.zh: 所以在番茄上我们或许还有一点提升空间。

cues.en: The point here is tomatoes are much, much harder to grow though than lettuce in indoor ag.
cues.zh: 但关键是，在室内农业里，番茄可比生菜难种得多。

cues.en: Now let's do an analysis of what we could do--and this is my final set of slides in this talk--
cues.zh: 现在我们来分析一下我们能做什么——这也是我这次演讲的最后一组幻灯片——

cues.en: what we could do with solar panels and LEDs so that we didn't have to use fossil fuels to get all that electricity.
cues.zh: 看看用太阳能板和LED能怎么做，从而不必靠化石燃料来获取所有这些电力。

cues.en: Let's analyze this.
cues.zh: 我们来分析一下。

cues.en: What we're going to compare--this is sunlight. If we do total energy in sunlight, it's 30 mega joules per meter² per day of total short wave energy
cues.zh: 我们要比较的是——这是阳光。如果计算阳光的总能量，每天每平方米的总短波能量是 30 兆焦耳，

cues.en: and 60 moles of photosynthetic photons per day. Now this is what drives the photosynthesis.
cues.zh: 以及每天 60 摩尔的光合光子。这才是驱动光合作用的东西。

cues.en: And the first step here is this is what drives solar panels.
cues.zh: 而这里的第一步，是这东西驱动太阳能板。

cues.en: So let's do this side first.
cues.zh: 那我们先看这一边。

cues.en: 60 moles comes through a greenhouse, 70% transmission. This is a good greenhouse. It's a design goal for a greenhouse,
cues.zh: 60 摩尔穿过温室，透射率 70%。这算是个好温室。这也是温室的设计目标，

cues.en: and obviously we get with this we get 42 moles, 70% of this, transmitted to the plant canopy.
cues.zh: 显然这样我们得到 42 摩尔，也就是其中的 70%，透射到植物冠层。

cues.en: Now let's analyze this side. First step, photovoltaic panels, 20% efficient.
cues.zh: 现在来分析这一侧。第一步，光伏板，效率 20%。

cues.en: So that's 30, goes to six moles per meter square per day. That is captured as electricity from the sun per meter² of solar panels.
cues.zh: 所以 30 会变成每天每平方米 6 摩尔。这就是每平方米太阳能板从太阳捕获到的电能。

cues.en: Now we take the electricity. Put it through LEDs. Our very best LEDs can get to three micromoles per Joule of photons.
cues.zh: 现在我们把这些电拿来。让它通过 LED。我们最好的 LED 能达到每焦耳 3 微摩尔光子。

cues.en: Micromoles of photons per Joule.
cues.zh: 每焦耳多少微摩尔光子。

cues.en: M is 10 to the six, this is 10 to the minus six, so this is three times six = 18.
cues.zh: M 是 10 的 6 次方，这个是 10 的负 6 次方，所以就是 3 乘 6 = 18。

cues.en: 18 moles of photons delivered to the plant canopy with solar photo takes. And it’s 42 here. This is a bigger number than this.
cues.zh: 靠太阳光向植物冠层输送 18 摩尔光子。这里则是 42。这个数字比那个大。

cues.en: It takes more than two times the area of solar panels to make the equivalent of what we could get in a greenhouse with nothing. Just a glass greenhouse.
cues.zh: 要用超过两倍面积的太阳能板，才能等效于一座空玻璃温室——里面什么都没有，只有玻璃——所能获得的效果。

cues.en: So I made a diagram to emphasize that point.
cues.zh: 所以我画了一张图来强调这一点。

cues.en: This is solar panels in a field. 2.3 acres of solar panels feeding electricity to light up one area.
cues.zh: 这是田野里的太阳能板。2.3 英亩的太阳能板发的电，只够照亮一块区域。

cues.en: So, we're not there for direct use of solar energy through LEDs.
cues.zh: 所以，我们还做不到通过 LED 直接利用太阳能。

cues.en: But, you say solar panels are getting better. LEDs are getting better. Now let's calculate the potential of this.
cues.zh: 但你说太阳能板在变好，LED 也在变好。现在我们来算算这其中的潜力。

cues.en: What if we peer into the future and look at what solar panels could be and what LEDs could be. Can we get this ratio better?
cues.zh: 如果我们展望未来，看看太阳能板和 LED 可能达到什么水平。我们能把这一比值做得更好吗？

cues.en: Here's the same graph potential. Kept this the same, 70%. We might get this higher with special coverings.
cues.zh: 这里是一样的潜力图。这个保持相同，70%。用特殊涂层我们也许能把它提高。

cues.en: But let's keep this side the same. Now we go to 30% solar panels.
cues.zh: 但这边先保持不变。现在我们看效率 30% 的太阳能板。

cues.en: Now these, the stuff we fly on satellites, they're expensive. They're 30%.
cues.zh: 这些就是我们装在卫星上的东西，很贵。效率是 30%。

cues.en: So it's possible to get these, and at some point in the future, we'll have consumer panels that are 30% efficient.
cues.zh: 所以这些是能搞到的，未来某个时候，我们会用上效率 30% 的消费级太阳能板。

cues.en: And the reason they're so efficient is they can use energy out here in shortwave energy by layering cells that photosynthesis can't use.
cues.zh: 它们效率这么高，是因为通过叠加电池层，可以利用短波部分的能量，而光合作用用不了这些能量。

cues.en: Photosynthesis uses this part of the curve and solar panels, by layering them, can use these low-energy, near-infrared photons.
cues.zh: 光合作用利用的是曲线上的这一部分，而太阳能板通过分层叠加，可以利用这些低能量的近红外光子。

cues.en: So they get to 30%.
cues.zh: 所以它们能达到30%。

cues.en: Now we've captured nine megajoules of electricity.
cues.zh: 现在我们捕获了9兆焦耳的电能。

cues.en: Now the theoretical maximum. if we had a 100% efficient LEDs, which we're really not going to get there, but we might get to 90-95%.
cues.zh: 再来看理论最大值。如果我们有100%效率的LED，虽然实际上达不到，但也许能达到90%到95%。

cues.en: We can get close. 9.7 times 4.7 = 42.
cues.zh: 我们可以接近。9.7乘4.7等于42。

cues.en: So potentially we can have a system where that's 1:1.
cues.zh: 所以有可能做出一个比例达到1:1的系统。

cues.en: The one acre of solar panels feeds one acre of plants and they don't have a greenhouse.
cues.zh: 一英亩太阳能板为一英亩植物供能，而且不用温室。

cues.en: Now this is the cost of building a greenhouse versus all these high efficiency solar panels and LEDs.
cues.zh: 现在比较一下建温室的成本，与所有这些高效太阳能板和LED的成本。

cues.en: This doesn't show economic, it just shows energy flow in this system.
cues.zh: 这并不能说明经济性，只是展示了这个系统中的能量流动。

cues.en: So one final slide. This is from a recent paper that is now in review with my colleagues, Paul Kusuma and Morgan Pattison.
cues.zh: 最后一张幻灯片。它来自一篇最近的论文，目前正与我的同事 Paul Kusuma 和 Morgan Pattison 一起接受审稿。

cues.en: It's called “From physics to fixtures to food: Potential efficacy of LEDs.”
cues.zh: 论文题目是“From physics to fixtures to food: Potential efficacy of LEDs”（从物理到灯具到食物：LED 的潜在效能）。

cues.en: This is peering into the future. These numbers come from the chip manufacturers of LEDs.
cues.zh: 这是在展望未来。这些数字来自 LED 芯片制造商。

cues.en: Not the ones that make the fixtures, just the ones that make the chip. How good can they get those chips?
cues.zh: 不是做灯具的厂商，只是做芯片的厂商。他们能把芯片做到多好？

cues.en: Here's the colors we use. We use blues, we use reds, we use far-reds, and we use whites.
cues.zh: 这是我们使用的颜色。我们用蓝光、红光、远红光，还有白光。

cues.en: And cool white is the most efficient of the whites. Look at these efficiencies now.
cues.zh: 冷白光在各类白光中效率最高。现在看看这些效率数据。

cues.en: This is watts of photosynthetic energy out, per watt of electricity in.
cues.zh: 这是每输入一瓦电能所输出的光合有效能量瓦数。

cues.en: Wow! 88% for blue LEDs. That is really impressive.
cues.zh: 哇！蓝光 LED 达到 88%。这确实令人惊叹。

cues.en: Whites are phosphor-converted blue. So they take blue with a phosphor, and we get white.
cues.zh: 白光是由荧光粉转换蓝光得到的。也就是用荧光粉处理蓝光，从而得到白光。

cues.en: So there's some loss in that, and so whites are 80%. And the reds are less, and the far-reds are less.
cues.zh: 这个过程中会有一些损耗，所以白光效率是 80%。红光的效率更低，远红光还要更低。

cues.en: Now this is energy. But remember energy doesn't drive photosynthesis, the number of photons do.
cues.zh: 现在这是能量。但记住，驱动光合作用的不是能量，而是光子的数量。

cues.en: So this column is the micromoles of photons per Joule.
cues.zh: 所以这一列是每焦耳的光子微摩尔数。

cues.en: Let me review this number. This is micromoles per second over joules per second.
cues.zh: 我来复核一下这个数字。这是每秒微摩尔数除以每秒焦耳数。

cues.en: And the seconds cancel, so it is just micromoles per Joule, and a Joule per second is a watt.
cues.zh: 秒会约掉，所以就是微摩尔每焦耳；而每秒1焦耳就是1瓦特。

cues.en: So it simplifies to micromoles per Joule.
cues.zh: 所以化简后就是微摩尔每焦耳。

cues.en: Look at these numbers, 3.3 up to 4. These are impressive numbers. We don't have fixtures this good yet,
cues.zh: 看这些数字，从3.3到4。这些数字很可观。我们还没有这么好的灯具，

cues.en: but on the horizon we could see where they could get this good for these colors of light.
cues.zh: 但未来有望看到，它们在这些颜色的光上能达到这么好的水平。

cues.en: Now I got a final box here that I haven't shown you yet. What's in that box?
cues.zh: 我这儿还有最后一个盒子没给你们看。盒子里是什么？

cues.en: If there's efficiency shown this way. Efficacy.
cues.zh: 如果效率是这样体现的。是效能。

cues.en: What about the cost of these? Which do you think is the most cost-effective, the easiest to make?
cues.zh: 那这些的成本呢？你们觉得哪种性价比最高、最容易制造？

cues.en: Most lighting, almost all lighting, is for humans. And so humans need white LEDs.
cues.zh: 大多数照明，几乎所有照明，都是给人用的。所以人类需要白光 LED。

cues.en: So, the white LEDs are much much cheaper, just because of economy of scale of this.
cues.zh: 所以白光 LED 便宜得多得多，就是因为它的规模经济。

cues.en: So now let's look at the price. Wow! 1x for whites. And we go to 10x for reds. And 30x for these.
cues.zh: 现在看看价格。哇！白光的是 1 倍。红光的是 10 倍。这些是 30 倍。

cues.en: These drive the cost of fixtures, that drive the cost of what we're going to do in indoor agriculture.
cues.zh: 这些会推高设备成本，而设备成本又决定室内农业的成本。

cues.en: So this is peering into the future and looking at what we can produce.
cues.zh: 所以这是在展望未来，看看我们能生产什么。

cues.en: All of our analysis indicates that leafy greens can be very cost-effective once we get the systems optimized.
cues.zh: 我们的所有分析都表明，一旦系统优化到位，叶菜类会非常有成本效益。

cues.en: Tomatoes would be much harder, and things like strawberries and broccoli are extremely difficult to ever produce without free sunlight.
cues.zh: 番茄会难得多，而像草莓和西兰花这样的作物，如果没有免费阳光，几乎不可能生产出来。

cues.en: Thanks for listening. I look forward to another video with you.
cues.zh: 感谢收听，期待在下个视频与你再见。
